Meta Ads

Facebook Ads Strategy to Increase Repeat Purchases for D2C Brands in India

By Aarush Chotaliya · 24 November 2026 · 9 min read

Getting a customer to buy your product for the first time is difficult. Getting them to come back and buy again is a different challenge altogether.

Think about a clothing brand spending ₹1,000 to acquire a customer. The customer places an order, receives the product and has a good experience. But what happens next? Does the brand have a plan to bring that customer back, or does it simply move on to finding the next buyer? This is something many D2C brands overlook.

A lot of attention goes into running Meta Ads, finding new audiences and generating orders. Meanwhile, thousands of previous customers are sitting in the database without any meaningful marketing communication.

For Indian D2C brands, particularly in clothing, cosmetics and lifestyle, this is an opportunity worth paying attention to. A well-planned Meta Ads strategy can help brands reconnect with previous buyers, introduce new products and encourage customers to shop again. Let's look at how to approach this.

1. Stop Focusing Only on New Customer Acquisition

One thing I've noticed about growing ecommerce businesses is that the pressure to acquire new customers never really stops. Every month, there is a new sales target, a new campaign and a new advertising budget. The team keeps looking for fresh audiences, testing creatives and trying to improve ROAS.

But how much attention is going towards customers who have already purchased? Imagine a cosmetics brand selling skincare products. Someone purchased a face wash today. There is a reasonable possibility that the customer may need another one in a few weeks or months.

Similarly, someone buying a shirt from a clothing brand might be interested in the brand's next collection. Yet many brands don't have a proper advertising strategy for these customers.

Instead of spending the entire marketing budget on acquiring new buyers, brands should also work on increasing the value of customers they have already acquired. This is where repeat purchase marketing becomes important.

2. Build Your Meta Ads Strategy Around Customer Behaviour

Not every customer should see the same advertisement. Someone who purchased yesterday has a different requirement from someone who purchased six months ago. Showing both customers the same discount advertisement doesn't necessarily make sense.

A better approach is to divide customers based on their purchase history and interactions with your brand.

For example:

  • First-time customers: They have purchased once. Introduce them to other products, explain your brand's range and give them a reason to return.
  • Repeat customers: These customers already know your brand. Show them new collections, complementary products or exclusive offers.
  • High-value customers: They have purchased multiple times or regularly spend more than other customers. Give them early access to new launches or premium collections.
  • Inactive customers: They haven't purchased in a while. Try reconnecting through new product launches, relevant offers or reminders about products they may like.

You can build relevant audiences using Meta Custom Audiences and eligible customer data from your ecommerce store. The important thing is to understand that customer behaviour should influence your advertising strategy.

3. How Clothing Brands Can Improve ROAS on Meta Ads

Clothing brands have an interesting advantage when it comes to repeat purchases. People don't usually buy just one piece of clothing and stop shopping forever. Their preferences change, seasons change and new collections keep coming in. However, that doesn't mean customers will automatically return to the same brand.

Brands need to give them a reason. Here are a few ways clothing businesses can approach this.

Promote New Collections to Existing Customers

Suppose someone purchased a pair of jeans from your store two months ago. Now your brand has launched a new collection of shirts and casual wear. Instead of spending additional money trying to find completely new audiences, you can create a campaign targeting relevant previous customers.

They already know your brand, so the advertisement can focus on what is new rather than introducing the business from scratch.

Try Product-Based Retargeting

A customer who purchased a particular product may be interested in something complementary. For example, if someone purchased a formal shirt, you could introduce matching trousers or accessories. Product catalogues and dynamic ads can help showcase relevant products, depending on the available customer and product data.

Don't Ignore Seasonal Opportunities

Indian customers shop differently during festive seasons, wedding seasons and end-of-season sales. Diwali, wedding collections and new seasonal launches give brands opportunities to reconnect with previous buyers.

Instead of creating the same promotional campaign every month, think about what your existing customers might actually be interested in purchasing.

Measure More Than Just First-Purchase ROAS

This is particularly important. A clothing brand might generate a good ROAS from Meta Ads but still struggle with profitability because of discounts, returns, shipping costs and product margins.

Along with ROAS, keep an eye on:

  • Customer acquisition cost (CAC).
  • Average order value (AOV).
  • Repeat purchase rate.
  • Customer lifetime value (LTV).
  • Contribution margin.
  • Revenue from returning customers.

There isn't one ideal ROAS for every clothing brand in India. A brand with healthy margins may be profitable at a different ROAS than a brand operating with heavy discounts. The objective should be profitable growth, not just a better-looking advertising dashboard.

4. How to Utilise AI Tools for Facebook Ads

Running Meta Ads becomes increasingly difficult when a brand starts managing multiple products, campaigns and advertising accounts. A performance marketer might spend hours checking campaign performance, reviewing creatives, preparing reports and figuring out what needs attention.

And then there is the repetitive work that happens every day. This is where AI tools for Facebook Ads can be useful. Rather than treating AI as something that simply generates advertising copy, businesses can use it to support different parts of their advertising workflow.

For example:

  • Campaign research: AI can help analyse available business and advertising data to identify products, audiences and campaign opportunities.
  • Creative development: It can help generate new creative concepts, advertising angles and variations for testing.
  • Performance analysis: AI can help identify changes in CTR, CPC, CPM, conversions and other campaign metrics.
  • Reporting: Instead of manually preparing reports every time, businesses can use automation to organise campaign performance data.
  • Optimisation: AI-powered systems can help identify underperforming campaigns and highlight opportunities for improvement.

Of course, AI shouldn't make every decision without context. A campaign that looks expensive on paper might still be profitable, depending on its contribution to the overall business. The real value comes from combining business understanding, accurate data and automation.

5. What Is the Best Software for D2C Brands?

As a D2C brand grows, its technology stack tends to grow with it. There is one platform for the online store, another for advertising, another for reporting and several other tools for managing different activities.

Eventually, founders find themselves switching between platforms just to understand what is happening in their own business. This creates another problem: information becomes scattered. Choosing the best software for D2C brands depends on what the business actually needs.

For a brand spending significantly on Meta Ads, some important things to consider are:

  • Can the software help with campaign research and planning?
  • Can it reduce manual campaign management?
  • Does it support creative development and testing?
  • Can it simplify performance reporting?
  • Does it provide useful optimisation insights?
  • Can it connect with the ecommerce store?

A tool shouldn't just add another dashboard to your business. It should solve an actual operational problem.

Conclusion: Your Next Customer Might Already Be in Your Database

Growing a D2C business isn't always about finding more customers. Sometimes, the opportunity is in building a better relationship with the customers you've already acquired.

If someone has purchased from your brand once and had a good experience, give them a reason to return. Introduce new products, understand their buying behaviour and communicate when it actually makes sense. Use Meta Ads retargeting, customer segmentation and AI-powered tools to make this process more organised.

And most importantly, don't measure your marketing success only by how many new customers you acquire. Pay attention to how many customers come back. That's an important part of building a sustainable D2C business.

Frequently asked questions

How can Meta Ads help increase repeat purchases?

Meta Ads can help brands reconnect with previous customers through retargeting, customer lists, product catalogues and personalised advertisements. Brands can promote new collections, complementary products and relevant offers to encourage another purchase.

What is the best Meta Ads strategy for clothing brands in India?

Clothing brands should combine new customer acquisition with campaigns targeting previous buyers. Promoting new collections, seasonal products and complementary items can help generate repeat orders. Measuring customer lifetime value alongside ROAS also helps businesses understand long-term profitability.

How to utilise AI tools for Facebook Ads?

AI tools can support campaign research, creative development, performance analysis, automated reporting and optimisation. They help reduce repetitive marketing work and allow teams to spend more time on strategy and decision-making.

What is a good ROAS for clothing brands on Meta Ads?

There is no fixed ROAS benchmark that works for every clothing brand. Profitability depends on product margins, advertising costs, shipping, returns, discounts and repeat purchases. Brands should calculate their break-even ROAS before deciding their advertising targets.

What is the best software for D2C brands?

The best software depends on the business's requirements. Brands should look for solutions that simplify advertising management, automate repetitive work, support reporting and provide actionable performance insights. ARINE is designed to help D2C brands automate key Meta Ads workflows.
